questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Utrecht due to its strong international reputation within veterinary medicine and its practical approach to teaching. The university is known for its high level of English and the close collaboration between students and teachers.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I was a little difficult, I got all the information straight from my contact person. However, I received some information very late, and only when I asked for it from the student counselor.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: On my first day, I was welcomed by a staff member who showed me around and helped me settle in. However, I did not receive any information about what is expected of the students, what we are allowed to do, or the routines of the hospital. I had to ask the other students about all of this, but they were all very helpful and understanding

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I was warmly welcomed by a staff member and met with the coordinator responsible for exchange students during the first week, who answered all my questions. However, I received the information about where to arrive on my first day rather late, which meant I had to send several emails to obtain the necessary details.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The Netherlands is currently experiencing a significant housing crisis, which made it challenging to find suitable accommodation, and it can be very expensive (1000-1500 euros pr month). I managed to secure housing through Airbnb.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend living off campus, as the campus is not really in the city. The public transportation system is excellent, and it is easy to get around by bike, so living off campus is not a problem. You can also look for housing in nearby cities, as it might be easier to find.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Because the stay was only 10 weeks, the university did not provide housing, but they did offer recommendations on where accommodation could be found

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a bit confusing. I received an email confirming my exchange spot and asking about my preferred subject, as well as instructions on uploading documents to the mobility service. However, there were issues getting the online Learning Agreement accepted because my start date didn’t match the regular semester dates. I had to contact them to find out what to do instead

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Both the Danish and the people from Utrecht were very good at answering any questions. However, the reply time was long.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The university was very accommodating, and upon my request, I was allowed to switch one week to another specialty that I found more interesting

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the instructions, and don't be afraid to ask for help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was a clinical rotation, with a high quality. You get to work with a lot of specialists.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is very similar, but is still done a little differently

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Companion animal hospital for 10 weeks, where I did: Diagnostic Imaging, Anesthesiology, soft tissue surgery, Cardiology, Emergency, Neurology, Internal ward, ophthalmology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Anesthesiology, Soft tissue surgery, Emergency, Ophthalmology. It was the rotation I got to do the most and learned the most.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I did not join any non-academic opportunities at the university, but I do know that the student association club plans a lot of activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the student associations club, they know what is going on, and can help you with recommendations

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Utrecht is a beautiful city with a lot of life, cafés, and activities to enjoy. I would also definitely recommend visiting Den Haag and Rotterdam, which are both really beautiful and easy to reach by train, making them perfect for a one-day trip. In most major cities in the Netherlands, you can join free walking tours, which is a great way to explore and get to know the city

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, as it is quite similar to Danish culture

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They are very nice and helpful; you just have to be open and not afraid to be the one starting the conversation.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language. The teachers and students are very good at English, though you need to remind them to speak English. It was a bit more challenging with the owners, but most of them were fine speaking English during the anamnesis

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: There is a very good work ethic, and people were generally very nice and helpful

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Don’t be afraid to ask for help.
2. Choose the rotations you find most interesting, but keep in mind that in those with more owner contact, you might miss some of it because it is in Dutch.
3. There are a lot of cool procedures and things we don’t see as much in Denmark, so don’t be afraid to say that you want to participate or ask if you can try.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It can seem a bit intimidating in the beginning, and sometimes they might discuss things that we in Denmark haven’t been taught much. Other times, there are topics we have studied in more depth than they have. So don’t be afraid to say that you’re not sure about something and ask them to explain it to you

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to see different ways of doing things and experiencing procedures I haven’t seen in Denmark, as well as learning from specialists and meeting the Dutch students

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting information about where I should meet and how to arrange my credit transfer

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
